solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Supplement taken around clubs creates unhealthy need

indicators.note: the supplement word is wrapped around the card-suit letter, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: an addition is something supplementary
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: A dietary supplement wrapped around clubs somehow breeds a craving.
explanation.definitionFit: A dependency on a drug or habit is a compulsive, harmful need.

clue.text: Tree more bare: bark initially removed

indicators.note: the opening letter of bark is taken away from the comparative word

parts.note: balder means more bare, having less hair

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word bark

explanation.surface: A tree stands more exposed once the start of its bark is stripped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bark' looks like part of the tree picture, but only its first letter, B, matters: it is taken from BALDER.
explanation.definitionFit: The alder is a common waterside tree of the birch family.

clue.text: Puzzle upset cover girl

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means the word for a cover is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: a lid is a cover
Emma is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A puzzle has upset a magazine cover girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cover girl' reads as one phrase, but the clue splits it: the cover is reversed and the girl follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilemma is a perplexing choice, a puzzle with no good way out.

clue.text: Royal household cool about second romance

indicators.note: about here means next to, so the word for cool sits beside the abbreviation for second

parts.note: a court is the household of a sovereign
hip means cool, fashionable

explanation.surface: A royal household is lukewarm about a second romance.
explanation.definitionFit: Courting is the wooing stage of a love affair, a romance before marriage.

clue.text: One freelanced working in European location

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: working suggests the letters are put to work in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone working freelance somewhere in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' looks like what the freelancer does, but it signals rearranging FREELANCED into LEDEFRANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ile-de-France is the region of France surrounding Paris.

clue.text: Surface on cloth sends pot wrong way

indicators.note: sends, together with wrong way, tells us the pot word is turned round
in a down entry going the wrong way means reading the word backwards, bottom to top

parts.note: a pan is a cooking pot

explanation.surface: Something on the cloth sends a pot off in the wrong direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Nap is the raised fuzzy surface of fibres on fabrics such as velvet.

clue.text: Band in hotel criminal guild protects

indicators.note: protects means the guild's letters wrap round and shelter the other piece

parts.note: a tong is a Chinese secret society, often criminal
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A band playing in a hotel enjoys the protection of a criminal gang.
explanation.definitionFit: A thong is a narrow strip of leather, a band or strap.

clue.text: Chuck cover over furniture

definitions.meaning: to chuck is to toss or hurl
a decorative blanket draped over a sofa or bed

explanation.surface: Throw a dust cover over the furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: To hurl is to chuck; a draped blanket on a settee is also so named.

clue.text: Gold coin forged — nothing for this banker

parts.note: OR is gold in heraldry

indicators.note: forged means the letters are hammered into a new form

parts.note: O is the zero or nothing shape

explanation.surface: A forged gold coin is worth nothing to a banker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banker' is a crossword joke for a river, something with banks, not a financier.
explanation.definitionFit: The Orinoco is a great South American river, so it has banks on both sides.

clue.text: Lass circling ancient sea gets first prize

indicators.note: circling means the lass word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a lass
old means ancient
Med is short for the Mediterranean Sea

explanation.surface: A girl sailing round an ancient sea wins top honours.
explanation.definitionFit: The winner of an Olympic event receives the top award, a gilded medal.

clue.text: Tortured soul immersed in river to purify

indicators.note: immersed in means the shuffled letters are dunked inside the river name

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain

indicators.note: tortured means twisted out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tormented soul is baptised in a river to cleanse it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tortured' yields LOUS, and 'immersed in' dunks it; the River Dee runs through Wales and Chester.
explanation.definitionFit: To rid of lice is a literal cleansing, here stretched to purify.

clue.text: Biased mate cunning one roped in

indicators.note: roped in means the pieces are lassoed inside the mate word

parts.note: a pal is a mate, a friend
art means cunning or craft
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A prejudiced friend has cunningly roped someone in.
explanation.definitionFit: Partial means favouring one side, prejudiced rather than impartial.

clue.text: Frenchman in bank about to send cash

indicators.note: about means the whole assembly is turned round and read backwards
in means the Frenchman's letter goes inside the bank word

parts.note: a tier is a bank, a row of seats or stage
M is short for Monsieur, a Frenchman

explanation.surface: A Frenchman at the bank is about to wire money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' suggests money but means a tier, a row; M goes in to give TIMER, then 'about' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: To remit is to transmit payment, as in remitting funds.

clue.text: Romeo in bits without line to submit in play

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the jumbled letters sit around the other pieces
in bits means broken to pieces, so the letters are reassembled

parts.note: to bow is to submit, give way

explanation.surface: Romeo goes to pieces in a play when he has no line to deliver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in bits' yields EROOM and 'without' means outside; 'play' is slack, not drama, despite Romeo.
explanation.definitionFit: Play means free movement or slack, the space allowed to move.

clue.text: Dog plus horse seen in spring

indicators.note: seen in means the pieces appear inside the spring word

parts.note: a bound is a leap, a spring
an asset is a plus, an advantage
H is slang for heroin, also called horse

explanation.surface: A dog and a horse are spotted in springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horse' is drug slang for heroin, abbreviated H; 'spring' is a jump, not the season.
explanation.definitionFit: This long-eared, short-legged breed is a hunting hound.

clue.text: Turkish commander edges away from infidel

indicators.note: the outer letters are stripped from the word for an unbeliever

parts.note: a pagan is a heathen, an infidel

explanation.surface: A Turkish officer edges away from an unbeliever.
explanation.definitionFit: An Aga was a military commander or chief officer in the Ottoman Empire.

clue.text: Castle hit — destroyed for sport

indicators.note: destroyed means the two words are knocked down and rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A castle hit and destroyed, perhaps as entertainment.
explanation.definitionFit: Track and field events such as running and jumping form this sport.

clue.text: Puzzling over piano, choirs retuned instrument

indicators.note: over means the puzzling word stretches across the other pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: hard means puzzling, difficult
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, soft

indicators.note: retuned means the letters are adjusted into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Choirs retune their voices over a piano, finding it puzzling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retuned' yields SICHOR and 'over' encloses; the piano is just a letter, not the instrument meant.
explanation.definitionFit: A keyboard instrument with plucked strings, popular in Baroque music.

clue.text: Fraud articles for those affording personal cover?

parts.note: cod means fake or a hoax
pieces are articles or items

explanation.surface: Fraudulent goods sold to people offering insurance cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'personal cover' sounds like insurance, but it is a coy reference to the pouch on old men's breeches.
explanation.definitionFit: These were pouches worn at the front of breeches in Tudor times, covering the groin.

clue.text: Grip wheel and make turn here

parts.note: a hairpin is a hair grip
to wheel is to turn or bend round

explanation.surface: Grip the steering wheel and turn here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grip wheel' paints a driver, but grip is a hair grip and wheel a curve.
explanation.definitionFit: A very sharp U-shaped curve in a road, where drivers must swing round.

clue.text: Do I lie with another having embraced sex appeal?

indicators.note: having embraced means the coupling word wraps round the other piece

parts.note: to mate is to pair up and lie with another
it is old slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: Do I sleep with someone else who has sex appeal?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' looks like an auxiliary verb but is the definition: to do someone is to impersonate them.
explanation.definitionFit: To do a celebrity is to mimic or impersonate them.

clue.text: Beer they say makes you sicken

indicators.note: they say means the word is as spoken, matching another in sound

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: People claim beer can make you ill.
explanation.definitionFit: To ail is to be unwell or to fall sick.

clue.text: Cunning Italian author entertains duke in style

indicators.note: entertains means the combined cunning and author letters hold the duke letter as a guest

parts.note: art means cunning, artfulness
Umberto Eco was an Italian novelist

explanation.surface: A crafty Italian writer entertains a duke in fine fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertains' works on the cunning word and the author together, not on the author alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A decorative design movement of the 1920s and 1930s, with bold geometric shapes.

clue.text: Beatles reformed to involve one hot girl

indicators.note: to involve means the jumbled band name takes the numeral inside
reformed means re-formed, the letters regrouped as a band might regroup

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: The Beatles re-form to bring in one attractive girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reformed' yields ELSABET and 'to involve' takes one in; the hot letter is simply appended.
explanation.definitionFit: Elisabeth is a female first name, so it suits a girl.

clue.text: Person in attendance cleared out home

indicators.note: in means the person word sits inside the remaining letters
cleared out means the word attendance is emptied, leaving only its outside letters

parts.note: bod is informal for a person

explanation.surface: An attendee clears out of their home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Person in attendance' reads as an attendee, but splits; 'cleared out' empties the word attendance.
explanation.definitionFit: An abode is a dwelling, the place where someone lives.

clue.text: Start denied playwright in Bury

indicators.note: the playwright's surname is denied its first letter

parts.note: Harold Pinter was a British playwright

explanation.surface: A playwright refused a start in the town of Bury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bury' looks like the Lancashire town, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter is to lay a corpse in a grave.

clue.text: Tint from crimper in Sevenoaks

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A hair colour from a hairdresser in Sevenoaks.
explanation.walkthrough: A crimper is slang for a hairdresser, and Sevenoaks is a town in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: A rinse is a temporary hair colouring, a light tint.

clue.text: Some American naiad running round house

indicators.note: round means the jumbled letters go round the house abbreviation
running means the letters move about freely into a new order

explanation.surface: A water nymph from America running round the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running' yields IDAAN and 'round' wraps it; a naiad is a water nymph, nothing American.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the potato-growing state is one particular kind of American.

clue.text: Raul Sanguineti beaten all ends up for nothing

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters are read from bottom to top
all ends means the final letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: A footballer beaten for a scoreless result.
explanation.definitionFit: A football score of zero, nothing at all.

clue.text: Morally impure relative Jane undressed

parts.note: an uncle is a relative

indicators.note: undressed means the name is stripped of its outer letters

explanation.surface: A lecherous relative strips Jane.
explanation.definitionFit: Unclean in a moral or ritual sense means sinful or defiled.

clue.text: Embarrassing display observed we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the word is spoken, matching another in sound

parts.note: seen means observed

explanation.surface: An embarrassing public display was observed and overheard.
explanation.definitionFit: Making a scene means an angry or emotional outburst in public.

clue.text: Attractive sort, see good chap over in valley

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning see or behold

indicators.note: in means the saint and the over letter go inside the valley word

parts.note: a dene is a narrow wooded valley
ST stands for saint, a good chap
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A charming type sees a good chap visiting the valley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attractive' is literal: the answer is a magnetic rock.
explanation.definitionFit: A naturally magnetic iron ore pulls metal toward it, so it is a magnetic sort.
